search_row.title: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes
search_row.statement: Under random mating and autosomal inheritance, selection drives parents to invest equally in sons and daughters, which gives a 1:1 sex ratio when the two cost the same.
search_row.math: ESS allocation: N_m c_m = N_f c_f; with c_m = c_f the unbeatable primary sex ratio is 1:1

fields.dct:source: Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Compare population sex-investment ratios (numbers times per-offspring cost) across species that meet the panmixia assumption, and test that experimentally perturbed sex ratios return toward equal investment.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: panmixia, autosomal control of the sex ratio, each offspring has one father and one mother, no local mate competition or sex-specific resource competition. Formal status: proved as an invasion (ESS) result (Shaw and Mohler 1953). Its own named exceptions (local mate competition, Hamilton 1967) are predicted deviations, not refutations.
